deadline.value: Fall 2027 application deadline is February 1, 2027 (Spring 2027: October 1, 2026; Summer starts not accepted). Note: most scholarships and fellowships go to Fall applicants; Graduate School First-Year Fellowship nominations close February 15.
deadline.quote: Fall 2027: February 1, 2027 | This program admits students for the Fall and Spring terms. Summer starts are not accepted.

also.quote: International students applying for the program should have all application materials into the Admissions Office at UCCS by February 1 for Fall Semester and by October 1 for Spring Semester. | Most scholarships and fellowships are given to Fall applicants, not Spring applicants.

gre_general.value: All GRE General sections are required for international applicants with at least 148 Quantitative; waived only for U.S. ABET CS bachelor's graduates (>= 3.0 GPA) or U.S. R1/R2 master's graduates (>= 3.0 GPA).
gre_general.quote: All sections of the Graduate Record Examination (GRE) are required, with at least 148 on the quantitative portion, unless one of the following conditions is satisfied: The applicant has a bachelor’s degree with a GPA of 3.0 or above from an ABET-accredited Computer Science or a closely related program from within the U.S. The applicant has a master’s degree in Computer Science or a closely related field with a GPA of 3.0 or above from an R1 or R2 institution from within the U.S.

also.quote: GRE: required, unless completed bachelor's degree with GPA of 3.0 or above from an ABET-accredited Comp Sci program or related program in the U.S. OR a master's degree with GPA of 3.0 or above from an R1 or R2 institution in the U.S.

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for Computer Science (ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics, and Psychology).
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

english_waiver.value: Computer Science specifies English proficiency waivers only for completing a degree in the U.S., so an English-medium degree from India requires TOEFL (80 / 4.5 new scale), IELTS (6.5), or Duolingo (115).
english_waiver.quote: A TOEFL score of 80 of higher, an ILETS of 6.5 or higher, or a Duolingo exam score of 115 will be required for proof of English Proficiency. If the student has completed a degree in the US, this requirement may be waived.

supervisor.value: Admission is decided by the PhD committee rather than an individual advisor's prior commitment, and students may begin qualifying exams before selecting an advisor; however, applicants must name 1-3 potential CS faculty advisors and justify fit in their goal/personal statement.
supervisor.quote: The PhD committee will review all applicants for admission | Complete a personal statement and within that personal statement name a potential advisor and justify your choice.

also.quote: The examining committee will be organized by the advisor if identified by the student, or by the program director if the advisor has not been chosen by the student.
Also include in your goal statement the three faculty member's names that you selected on page 4 and describe why you feel they would be a good fit for you as your advisor.

funding.value: Funding is competitive rather than guaranteed: students can apply directly to the department for RA/TA positions, which can pair with Graduate School Tuition Matching Grants (up to $8,000/yr) or competitive Graduate School PhD Grants (up to $26,000/yr) and First-Year Fellowships ($6,000/yr, mainly Fall admits).
funding.quote: For financial aid consideration, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Most scholarships and fellowships are given to Fall applicants, not Spring applicants.

also.quote: Research/Teaching Assistantships may be available, and are used for requesting financial assistance from the department - please contact the department directly for the RA/TA application.

Awards in any amount of up to $26,000 per year, or $13,000 per semester, may be processed by the Office of Financial Aid. | Resident and nonresident graduate students, including international students, are eligible for this grant.

entry_route.value: Admits holders of a bachelor's or master's degree in CS or a closely related field with >= 3.3 GPA and prerequisite math/CS coursework; bachelor's entrants may earn an M.S. along the way to the 60-credit Ph.D.
entry_route.quote: The student holds a bachelor's degree in computer science or a master's degree in computer science or closely related field from a college or university of recognized standing. A student who is admitted without a master's degree may earn that degree as a part of the Ph.D. studies.

notes: Covers both Computer Science, Ph.D. and the Department of Computer Science's companion Cybersecurity, Ph.D. (Security, Ph.D.; https://eas.uccs.edu/academics/programs/security-phd), which shares the same February 1 Fall deadline, GRE General (>= 148Q, same U.S. waiver rules), TOEFL 80 / IELTS 6.5 / Duolingo 115 (US-degree waiver), >= 3.3 GPA, 60-credit structure, and BS-or-MS entry route (plus a 3-month operational security internship/publication/CISSP requirement). Graduate School table lists 4.5 on the post-1/21/2026 TOEFL 1-6 scale (80 prior).
name: Computer Science, Ph.D. (and Cybersecurity, Ph.D.)
